findings.claim: Gate the remedy panel on a repeat failure, not every blocker: alternatives the brief omits are (a) finder ships acceptance criteria + invariant + test skeleton with the finding, (b) one solver, not a panel of three, (c) the worker must propose-then-code in the same wave, and (d) do nothing beyond a better worker brief. Triggering only when a fix has already failed once (F91-1/F91-2 are exactly that) captures most value at a fraction of the 3x consultation cost.
findings.trigger: Coordinator must choose between the proposed panel, a cheaper finder-brief improvement, and a single solver, with no data on which produces verified fixes.

evidence.observation: Pass 1 had 3 blockers + 5 findings, the worker fixed all eight, pass 2 HOLD again with two 'remaining case' findings: the failure mode is a failed fix, not a missing first remedy.

findings.verification: Pilot on the four F91 findings: record for each whether a solver proposal was adopted unmodified, partly, or rejected, and whether the implementing pass closed it. Compare against the pass-1-to-pass-2 re-failure baseline.
findings.remedy: Add an automatic offer only on HOLD where a finding supersedes or reopens a prior one. Run a single-solver pilot for one release and measure adoption rate and re-failure rate before building panels, exclusion, or scoring.

findings.claim: Q1: finder/solver separation is sound, but verification must be dual-key: the solver's shipped test is the primary evidence, the finder confirms the original trigger is closed, and a third member adjudicates only on dispute. Finder alone rejects foreign fixes and confirms its own frame; a solver-written test alone encodes the solver's wrong assumption as truth; a third verifier alone lacks trigger context.
findings.trigger: A solver from another lab, possibly pack-only with no repo access, proposes a fix the finder did not frame; someone must decide it closes the original trigger.

evidence.observation: The pass-2 findings are themselves 'the fix closed the simple case, this is the remaining case', i.e. implementer-side tests already encoded the implementer's frame once.

findings.verification: On the pilot, log finder/solver-verifier disagreements: the rate at which the shipped test passes but the finder still reproduces the trigger measures test-only verification failure.
findings.remedy: Finder states acceptance criteria (evidence that closes the finding) at raise time, before seeing proposals. Solver ships the named test. Finder verifies against its own criteria; disagreement or a second failure escalates to a third member. Solvers see claim and trigger but not the finder's one-line remedy, to avoid anchoring.

findings.claim: Q2: the minimal proposals[] record is {finding_id, proposer{provider, model, consult_id}, base_commit, approach, locations[], invariant, patch_sketch, test{name, drives, asserts}, risks, confidence}; the coordinator adds {status: adopted|rejected, reason} and the existing finding status flow proposed|implemented|verified does the rest. No new ledger is needed.
findings.trigger: A remedy consultation returns free text that the coordinator must store, choose from, and later credit, inside a files-are-the-record ledger.

evidence.observation: Brief states findings[].remedy, prior_findings[] statuses, panel roles, routing, packs and findings.json already exist; only proposals[] storage and a remedy purpose are new.

findings.verification: Round-trip one pilot consultation: proposals land in findings.json, coordinator marks adopted/rejected with reason, `c3 findings` shows the choice, and no step fires without an explicit coordinator command.
findings.remedy: Store proposals verbatim under findings[].proposals[] keyed by finding id, generated brief = finding record + pack of located code and existing tests at base_commit. Must NOT be automated: adoption, merging, implementation, verification/closure, and the decision to spend the window. Vendor exclusion should prefer a different model instance, not hard-exclude a lab, since vendor is a weak proxy for independence and may exclude the best solver.

findings.claim: Q3/F91-1 remedy: move attempt derivation and resumability revalidation inside claim_for_spawn under the admission lock. claim_for_spawn (mod.rs:747) currently only rejects a different live owner and unconditionally sets running; resume_once (mod.rs:1142) computes n before the lock; do_resume_foreground (mod.rs:1386) checks status/exhaustion on a pre-lock record.
findings.trigger: Two resumes pass pre-lock checks; the first finishes (done) or exhausts the cap while the second is paused before claim_for_spawn, which then resurrects it with a stale attempt number.

evidence.observation: claim_for_spawn rereads the record under admission_lock but checks only other-live-run and live-owner before writing running with the caller-supplied attempt.
n = quota.resumes + 1 is computed at line 1142, before claim_for_spawn acquires the lock at line 1146; status and exhausted checks at 1386-1399 use the earlier record.

findings.verification: New tests claim_for_spawn_rejects_terminal_and_exhausted (drive claim_for_spawn on done and on quota+exhausted records, assert Err and run.json unchanged) and claim_for_spawn_derives_attempt_from_locked_record (bump quota.resumes on disk after the caller's snapshot, assert the claimed attempt follows the locked value). Plus the barrier integration fixture from RC1 of handoff 91: delayed second resume refuses with no second launch marker.
findings.remedy: Change claim_for_spawn to take the caller's expectation (resumable statuses, max_resumes) instead of a precomputed attempt: under the lock, reread, refuse if status is not resumable, if quota.exhausted or resumes >= max, or if a different live owner holds it, then derive attempt = locked quota.resumes + 1 and write running in the same locked write. Pre-lock checks stay only as fast-fail UX. Invariant: no spawn unless the locked record was resumable at the claim instant, and attempt numbers are monotone in locked state.

findings.claim: Q3/F91-2 remedy: make admission fail closed on uninspectable records. read_record (record.rs:137) maps every fs::read error to Ok(None), run_dirs (record.rs:187) returns [] on read_dir failure and flattens entry errors, and live_run/other_live_run (record.rs:211/223) discard read errors via .ok(), so a live worker whose run.json is unreadable is invisible to the one-live-worker guard.
findings.trigger: A worker is alive while a second process can take the admission lock but cannot read the live run.json, or hits an enumeration/entry error; the guard sees no live run and launches a second worker.

evidence.observation: Err(_) => return Ok(None) at lines 139-142 swallows PermissionDenied identically to NotFound.
read_dir failure returns empty vec, entries iterate with flatten(), and live_run/other_live_run chain .ok().flatten() so parse/read errors read as absence.

findings.verification: New tests read_record_distinguishes_notfound_from_unreadable (missing dir yields Ok(None); a run.json made unreadable, e.g. replaced by a directory, yields Err) and admission_refuses_when_candidate_uninspectable (other_live_run/live_run return Err and claim_for_spawn refuses before writing running). Plus the RC1 denied-read fixture with a live blocking worker: second same-task command refuses with no launch marker.
findings.remedy: Distinguish error kinds: only ErrorKind::NotFound maps to Ok(None); all other read errors, plus directory enumeration and entry errors, propagate as Err. Change run_dirs, live_run and other_live_run to return Result and make both admission callers (run() start path and claim_for_spawn) refuse admission on Err. Invariant: admission proceeds only when every candidate record was inspected or confirmed absent; uninspectable state is a refusal, never an empty list. Parse errors already return Err and keep doing so.

findings.claim: Q3/F91-4 remedy: require affirmative terminal evidence per engine. summarize_events (record.rs:544) sets is_error=false unless is_error is exactly true, so a bare {"type":"result"} reads as Claude success; terminal_outcome (engines.rs:504) sets saw_completed on a Codex agent_message item, and the existing unit test at engines.rs:651 enshrines agent_message-only as Success.
findings.trigger: Exit-zero launcher emits only {"type":"result"} (Claude) or only an item.completed agent_message (Codex) and ends; the run is recorded done with no successful terminal event.

evidence.observation: Any result line sets has_result=true; is_error becomes true only for boolean true, absent included. Claude maps has_result && !is_error to Terminal::Success.
item.completed with an agent_message item sets saw_completed exactly like turn.completed; test terminal_outcome_reads_the_stream asserts Success for an agent_message-only stream.

findings.verification: Update terminal_outcome_reads_the_stream: agent_message-only Codex stream and bare-result Claude stream now yield Terminal::None (hence died via classify_attempt), while subtype success + is_error:false and turn.completed still yield Success. Add classify-level cases mirroring RC3 of handoff 91 for both engines at exit zero.
findings.remedy: Claude: add has_success_result to EventSummary, set only when subtype == "success" and is_error is explicitly Some(false); terminal_outcome returns Success only from that field, Error on an explicit error result, else None. Codex: delete the agent_message arm so only turn.completed sets saw_completed; agent_message keeps feeding report extraction in summarize, which is a separate path. classify_attempt already fails closed on Terminal::None, so no caller change is needed. Invariant: done requires the engine's own successful terminal event, never the absence of an error marker.

findings.claim: Q4: credit must be split, delayed, and denominated. Finder earns finder credit when a finding is verified real at closure; solver earns solver credit only when an adopted proposal is implemented and verified without material redesign (partly when the coordinator had to rework it). Adoption alone earns nothing scoreable, so raising easy blockers cannot farm solver or finder credit.
findings.trigger: Router learns from adoption/verification marks; a finder could raise trivial blockers, or a solver could win adoptions with confident but unverifiable proposals.

evidence.observation: Brief proposes adoption marks feed the router as a second score dimension; adoption is coordinator taste, verification is ground truth, and the two passes show findings vary widely in severity and recurrence.

findings.verification: Backfill-score the two acceptance passes: check that credit lands only on the verified F89 closures, that the reopened F89-2/F89-3/F89-8 yield recurrence-weighted rather than fresh credit, and that no score moves on adoption alone.
findings.remedy: Keep three separate router dimensions (finder, solver, verifier), each updated only at verified closure, weighted by severity and by whether the finding is a recurrence of a prior fix. The denominator counts rejected and duplicate findings against the finder, and rejected proposals against the solver, so volume without verification dilutes rather than accumulates. Require a minimum sample before solver routing outweighs the default roster.

findings.claim: The reopen pattern (F89-2→F91-1, F89-3→F91-3, F89-8→F91-4) is a verification gap, not a remedy gap: fixes were marked fixed without a test that drives the finder's trigger. A remedy panel alone will not close the loop; a closing-test obligation should accompany or precede it.
findings.trigger: A blocker is fixed from a one-line remedy, marked fixed by inspection, and the next pass reports 'the fix closed the simple case, this is the remaining case'.

evidence.observation: F89-2/3/8 are still-open with notes that the simple case closed while the claimed residual case remains; F89-1/6/7 were accepted 'by inspection'.
The brief itself describes pass-2 findings as 'the fix closed the simple case, this is the remaining case' of the pass-1 blockers.

findings.verification: Audit the wave10a fix commit for tests that encode each pass-1 trigger; expect triggers to be absent from the test names/fixtures.
findings.remedy: Require every finding to ship a deterministic reproduction test of its stated trigger before status can move past proposed/implemented; the remedy panel then designs against that test. Gate panel funding on findings that supersede an earlier finding. Keep the cheap path for first-time findings.

findings.claim: Verifier role: the solver's shipped reproduction test is the primary verifier, confirmed by the finder's next pass; a third panel member as verifier is redundant latency. 'Verified' must mean a green trigger reproduction, not the finder's taste.
findings.trigger: A foreign fix is correct but the finder's frame rejects it, or the finder accepts a fix that never reproduces the trigger; either way one party's judgment decides.

evidence.observation: The finder's own acceptance criteria are already machine-checkable observations (RC1-RC3 style), not opinions.
A third member costs a full consultation and re-derives what the reproduction test encodes.

findings.verification: Take one adopted proposal, implement only its test first, and confirm the finder's next pass verdict is determined by that test's result.
findings.remedy: Roles: finder raises and states acceptance criteria; solvers propose (design+locations+test); coordinator adopts; verification = the solver's test green on the exact trigger plus the finder's next pass. Seat a second solver as tie-break when the finder disputes an adopted fix. Do not add a verifier seat.

findings.claim: Minimal proposals[] record and workflow that fit the files-are-the-record ledger, with adoption choice, verified status, exclusion policy and panel opening explicitly left manual.
findings.trigger: A HOLD with blockers is routed to a remedy panel and its output must be stored, chosen among, and later judged.

evidence.observation: The brief describes findings[].remedy, prior_findings status, --role/--roles, packs and c3 findings status transitions as already existing.
Not read (6-call budget); the proposals[] ingest is assumed to mirror findings[].

findings.verification: Draft one remedy reply for F91-1 by hand into findings.json and run c3 findings to confirm the status transitions cover proposed|adopted|rejected without schema breakage.
findings.remedy: findings[].proposals[]: {finding_id, proposer{provider,model,consult_id}, approach, locations[], patch_sketch, test{name,drives}, risks[], confidence, status, decided_by, decided_reason}. Brief = finding record + pack of located code and nearby tests; --exclude-vendor <finder and previous fixer>. Never automate adoption, verified status, exclusion policy, or opening a panel.

findings.claim: Remedy for F91-1: claim_for_spawn must be the single authority — under admission_lock it revalidates permitted status (not done/artifact_error), quota.exhausted==false, and live-owner, then computes the next attempt from that same locked record; resume_once must drop its pre-lock attempt computation and use the returned attempt. Invariant: authorization and attempt generation derive from one locked record state; stale claims refuse without spawning.
findings.trigger: Two resume commands pass pre-lock checks; the second is delayed until after the first reaches done or exhausted=true; the second then claims and writes running with a stale attempt number.

evidence.observation: claim_for_spawn only rejects another live run / different live owner, then unconditionally writes running with the caller-supplied attempt.
resume_once computes n = quota.resumes+1 from an unlocked read before calling claim_for_spawn.
Status/exhaustion checks run before resume_env/resume_once, outside the lock (per F91-1 evidence; not re-read at those lines).

findings.verification: Test resume_refuses_stale_claim_after_completion: barrier the second launcher before claim; let the first reach done (and in a second case exhausted=true); require the delayed resume to exit nonzero with 'already completed'/'exhausted', no new .events-resume-* file, and an unchanged attempt field.
findings.remedy: Change claim_for_spawn to take no attempt argument: under the lock reread the record, assert resumable status and !exhausted and not already live under another owner, compute n from the locked quota, write running(pid,start,n), return the record. resume_once uses rec.attempt from the return value. Keep the pre-lock checks as early-out UX only.

findings.claim: Remedy for F91-3: replace unwrap_or_default on attempt/aggregate event reads with propagated read errors routed to finish_artifact_error, and move per-attempt temp-file deletion to after write_record succeeds. Invariant: unreadable source bytes are never replaced by empty content and never deleted; the run ends artifact_error with bytes retained.
findings.trigger: A resumed child writes a valid successful stream; reading .events-resume-N.jsonl fails while removal is still possible, or the append succeeds but the events.jsonl read inside refresh_artifacts fails transiently.

evidence.observation: attempt_events/attempt_stderr use unwrap_or_default; temp files are removed at 1192-1193 right after append, before refresh and write_record.
refresh_artifacts reads events.jsonl with unwrap_or_default and writes the resulting report without surfacing a read error.

findings.verification: Test resume_event_read_failure_keeps_attempt_bytes: inject read failure on the attempt temp file and, separately, on events.jsonl before refresh; require nonzero exit, status artifact_error, the temp file still present with the child's bytes, and report.md not rewritten empty.
findings.remedy: read_to_string(...).map_err(...) for both attempt files and the aggregate; on error call finish_artifact_error and return, keeping temp files. Delete temp files only after refresh_artifacts and write_record both succeed. Treat missing events.jsonl as empty only when the record has no prior attempts; a read error never overwrites report.md.

findings.claim: Remedy for F91-4: terminal_outcome must require affirmative success — Claude Success only on a result with is_error explicitly boolean false (absent is_error yields None/Error), Codex Success only on turn.completed (an agent_message item.completed is content, not completion). Invariant: done requires affirmative explicitly-successful terminal evidence; partial/ambiguous terminals fail closed as died.
findings.trigger: An exit-zero launcher emits only {"type":"result"} for Claude, or only an item.completed agent_message for Codex, with no successful turn terminal.

evidence.observation: Claude maps has_result with is_error false to Success; Codex sets saw_completed for agent_message item.completed as well as turn.completed.
An existing unit test expects Success for a Codex agent_message-only stream (per F91-4 evidence).
classify_attempt turns Terminal::Success + exit 0 into done; tightening terminal_outcome therefore blocks false done.

findings.verification: Test terminal_outcome_requires_affirmative_success driving the two stated streams plus an integration run with exit-zero fake launchers requiring status died, never done; flip the agent_message-only unit expectation.
findings.remedy: In terminal_outcome: Claude Success iff a result line has is_error present and equal to false; Codex drop the agent_message arm from saw_completed, keep turn.completed only, still erroring on turn.failed. Keep summarize()'s message extraction independent of Terminal. Update the unit test that currently codifies the weak behavior.

findings.claim: Scoring design: solver credit = one adoption point + one verification point per finding; finder credit is severity-weighted, requires the finding to survive a fix attempt and ship a reproduction test, and is discounted when the finding merely supersedes the finder's own prior finding; all scores derive from coordinator actions, never self-report.
findings.trigger: A finder raises many easy or self-superseding blockers to farm solver/finder scores, or a solver floods proposals per finding.

evidence.observation: The sketch proposes adoption marks as a second router dimension and per-consult usefulness ratings already exist.
Three of four pass-2 findings supersede the finder's own pass-1 findings — exactly the pattern a supersedes discount should price.

findings.verification: Replay the 0.2.3 acceptance history through the scoring rules and check the finder's score rises less for the three self-superseding findings than for independent ones.
findings.remedy: Add a solver dimension keyed on adopted/verified, capped at one point per finding; weight finder credit by severity and a reproduction test being present, applying a supersedes-of-own-finding discount. Take ratings from the coordinator's ledger entries (useful, adopted, test result) so neither finder nor solver can self-credit.

findings.claim: Verify a remedy mechanically, not with a third reviewer: the solver ships a failing-before/green-after test the coordinator runs, and the finder only replays its own trigger (binary closed/not-closed, never judging designs). Run solvers only on blockers and batch all blockers of one pass into a single remedy consultation.
findings.trigger: Three model consultations per blocker at ~9-16% of the finder's window each, while pass 2 shows the real failure is enumeration of error paths, not fix design.

evidence.observation: Two of four findings are explicitly 'the fix closed the simple case, this is the remaining case' (supersedes F89-2, F89-3, F89-8) — missed cases, not design disagreements.
Cost per pass ~280 s and 9-16% of the window; worker wave 40-60 min between passes.

findings.verification: Compare blocker closure rate and window spend of one release using the self-adversarial worker pass + single batched remedy consultation against the 3-solver panel design.
findings.remedy: Pin the verifier to two gates: a shipped failing test the coordinator executes, plus a narrow finder trigger replay. Before building panel-of-solvers machinery, try one release where the worker brief mandates enumerating every error return and race window in touched functions; escalate to solvers only if blockers still survive.

findings.claim: Minimal proposals[] record: {consult_id, member, approach, locations[], patch_sketch, test, risks, confidence, status proposed|adopted|rejected, reason}, stored in findings.json; pack = the named functions, their callers, existing tests and the run.json schema. Never automate: blocker realness, adoption choice, rejection wording, worker launch.
findings.trigger: Designing the remedy purpose without a record shape would fork the files-are-the-record ledger into per-consultation side files.

evidence.observation: findings[].remedy, prior_findings per-id status, roles, router ratings keyed by consult_id, and pack already exist to build on.
Statuses proposed|implemented|verified|rejected already exist, so proposals[] needs only the adoption state machine layered on the same file.

findings.verification: Review the patch adding proposals[] against findings.json's existing write path: one file, one writer (the coordinator), statuses settable by id.
findings.remedy: Extend findings.json only; generate the brief from the finding record plus a pack of located functions, callers and tests; leave adoption, rejection reasons and worker launches as coordinator-only actions.

findings.claim: F91-1 remedy: validate permitted state, exhaustion, live owner and expected attempt generation INSIDE claim_for_spawn under the admission lock; compute the resume number n from the locked reread, not the caller's stale record, and reject a stale claim instead of overwriting it.
findings.trigger: Two concurrent resumes both pass the pre-lock quota/exhausted checks in do_resume_foreground; the loser claims after the winner finished or exhausted the cap and writes `running` with a stale attempt number.

evidence.observation: The locked reread only rejects a live other run and a foreign live owner, then unconditionally writes running with the caller's attempt; no status, exhaustion or generation recheck.
resume_once computes n from a record read before acquiring the lock, then claims.
Status and exhausted checks run before resume_env/resume_once on the caller's record.

findings.verification: Test `resume_claim_rejects_stale_generation`: call resume_once with a rec whose attempt is bumped (or status set done) after n is computed; expect Err naming the state change, no `running` write, no child-launch marker.
findings.remedy: Change claim_for_spawn to take expected_status (quota|timeout|waiting_quota) and expected_attempt; under the lock reread, require status matches and not exhausted, derive n = q.resumes+1 from that record, return a typed StaleState error on mismatch; resume_once uses the returned record's n. Invariant: every `running` claim derives from a record read under the admission lock with a monotone per-record attempt number.

findings.claim: F91-2 remedy: make read_record, run_dirs, live_run and other_live_run error-propagating — only a confirmed NotFound means absence; any unreadable or unparseable candidate record makes admission refuse. Invariant: a start/resume proceeds only when every candidate record is positively readable or positively absent.
findings.trigger: A live worker's run.json is unreadable (denied ACL) or a work/ enumeration fails while another same-task command takes the admission lock: today it sees no live run and launches a second worker.

evidence.observation: Any std::fs::read error returns Ok(None), so access failures look like a vanished record.
run_dirs returns [] on read_dir failure; live_run and other_live_run drop record errors via .ok().flatten().
claim_for_spawn errors only when read_record yields None ('vanished'), i.e. it cannot distinguish unreadable from absent either.

findings.verification: Test `admission_refuses_when_record_unreadable`: live pending record plus a deny-read ACL on its run.json; a second `c3 work` start must refuse naming the unread record before any launch marker (RC2).
findings.remedy: read_record: Err on any read error except NotFound; run_dirs -> Result<Vec<(i64,PathBuf)>,String> treating only a NotFound root as empty; live_run/other_live_run return Result and callers convert inspection errors into refusal. Keep the ghost-reaping side effect (pending+not-live -> died) only on successfully parsed records.

findings.claim: F91-3 remedy: propagate event-file read errors instead of unwrap_or_default; delete per-attempt files only after their bytes were read AND durably appended; refresh_artifacts returns Err on an events.jsonl read failure BEFORE writing report.md, so a good report is never replaced by an empty one and a run can never finish `done` from unread artifacts.
findings.trigger: A resumed child writes a valid success stream but the tmp events read fails, or events.jsonl becomes transiently unreadable during refresh_artifacts.

evidence.observation: Attempt events/stderr use unwrap_or_default; files are removed right after append_resume succeeds, so a read failure silently appends nothing and deletes the source.
refresh_artifacts defaults a failed events.jsonl read to empty input and still writes the resulting report.
The record then takes the status classified earlier from the (possibly empty) attempt stream, including done.

findings.verification: Tests `resume_keeps_attempt_files_when_read_fails` (read failure on tmp events -> artifact_error, tmp files retained, events.jsonl unchanged) and `refresh_never_empties_report_on_read_failure` (events.jsonl read failure -> Err before any report write).
findings.remedy: Replace both unwrap_or_default reads with `?`; move the tmp deletions after classify_attempt consumes the same in-memory bytes and append_resume returns Ok; in refresh_artifacts read events.jsonl with `?` before any write. Invariant: no artifact source is removed or overwritten until its bytes are durably incorporated; any read failure is terminal artifact_error with a non-zero exit.

findings.claim: F91-4 remedy: success requires affirmative terminal evidence — Claude: a result object whose is_error is present and false (a bare {"type":"result"} is Terminal::None); Codex: only `turn.completed` sets success, an agent_message item.completed only feeds message extraction. Absence fails closed (`died`), keeping classify_attempt's exit-0 conjunction unchanged.
findings.trigger: An exit-zero fake launcher emits only a bare Claude result, or only a Codex item.completed agent_message without turn.completed.

evidence.observation: Claude maps has_result && !is_error to Success; Codex sets saw_completed for an agent_message item.completed as well as turn.completed.
The finder reports record.rs:544-551 defaults is_error to false when the field is absent; I did not re-read those lines (read budget).

findings.verification: Tests `claude_bare_result_is_died` and `codex_agent_message_without_turn_completed_is_died`: drive terminal_outcome with the two RC3 streams plus exit 0 and require Terminal::None -> `died`, never `done`.
findings.remedy: In the Claude arm require an explicit is_error==false on the result for Success; in the Codex arm stop setting saw_completed on agent_message item.completed and let summarize use it only for report text; update the existing unit test that currently expects Success for the agent_message-only stream. Invariant: Success <=> affirmative successful terminal event, independent of process exit code.

findings.claim: Q4 scoring: add a second router dimension `solver` beside `finder`. Solver points: adopted +1, verified (shipped test green AND finder confirms the trigger closed) +2, adopted-but-reblocked −1, rejected 0. A finder's finding counts toward its finder score only when a later pass closes it without regression; never-ending or phantom blockers stop scoring. Proposal adoption/rejection by the coordinator must not move solver scores — only verified outcomes do.
findings.trigger: Without outcome-gated credit, a finder can farm easy blockers and a loud solver can farm adoptions that the next pass overturns.

evidence.observation: Ratings useful yes|partly|no per consult_id already exist; the sketch proposes a solver dimension but no anti-gating rule.
A reviewer x purpose x topic score can host a second dimension without schema change; the closure signal must come from prior_findings status transitions.

findings.verification: Inspect the router table after one release with the rule: a finder whose blockers never reach verified shows a falling useful-rate, and solver scores track verified closures only.
findings.remedy: Credit on state transitions in findings.json: finder score matures at verified, solver score at adopted->verified; weight each by blockers-per-pass-to-closure so cheap easy blockers dilute rather than inflate the finder score.

findings.claim: Default to test-first worker briefs with the finder's requested checks as acceptance criteria (options O1+O2); escalate to a remedy panel (O3) only when the same finding survives two fix passes, because pass-2 evidence shows a verification gap, not a design gap.
findings.trigger: Any acceptance HOLD whose findings are 'the fix closed the simple case' of an earlier blocker.

evidence.observation: F91-1 and F91-3 supersede F89-2/F89-3 as remaining cases; Astra supplied executable checks RC1-RC3 that were never run between passes.

evidence.reference: brief section 'The situation that prompted this panel'
evidence.observation: 280s and 9-16% window per pass; remedy panels triple consultation cost per blocker.

findings.verification: Run RC2 to confirm workers can execute tests in-tree; if yes, pilot O1 on the next blocker and compare pass count to closure against the 0.2.3 loop.
findings.remedy: Brief the worker with the finding's trigger plus a mandatory failing test first; the finder verifies the test on the next pass. Reserve the solver panel for repeat failures.

findings.claim: The minimal proposals record is {proposer, approach, locations, patch_sketch, test, risks, confidence, status, reason} stored in findings.json under the finding id; adoption, rejection reasons, the decision to spend the window, and the verified flip must stay manual.
findings.trigger: Designing the remedy purpose and its ledger footprint.

evidence.observation: Brief lists existing findings[].remedy, prior_findings, panel roles, routing, packs; coordinator's sketch already stores proposals under the finding id.

findings.verification: Schema-review the proposed record against crates/c3/src/consult/ ingestion and `c3 findings` status transitions in a follow-up consult.
findings.remedy: Add findings[].proposals[] as plain JSON in the existing findings store; add purpose `remedy` with vendor exclusion and a pack of finding record + located code + existing tests. Never auto-adopt or auto-verify.

findings.claim: Proposed remedy for F91-1: claim_for_spawn must validate status, exhaustion and expected attempt generation from the record it rereads under the admission lock, and compute the next attempt from that locked record.
findings.trigger: A delayed resume passes pre-lock checks, then claims a record that became done or quota-exhausted, reusing a stale attempt number.

evidence.observation: The locked reread checks only other live runs and a different live owner, then unconditionally sets running with the caller-supplied attempt.

findings.verification: New test resume_after_terminal_refused: barrier before the second claim; first attempt reaches done, separately quota-exhausted; the delayed resume refuses with no child-launch marker and an unchanged run.json.
findings.remedy: Change claim_for_spawn to take expected_attempt; under the lock refuse when the reread record is terminal, quota.exhausted, or rec.attempt + 1 != expected_attempt; set rec.attempt = rec.attempt + 1 from the locked record.

findings.claim: Proposed remedy for F91-2: only a confirmed NotFound may count as an absent record; every other inspection error must propagate to admission, which refuses.
findings.trigger: A live worker's run.json cannot be read (permissions) or its directory cannot be enumerated; a second start or resume skips the live run.

evidence.observation: read_record maps every fs::read error to Ok(None); run_dirs returns empty on enumeration failure and flattens entry errors; live_run and other_live_run discard record errors.

findings.verification: New test admission_refuses_on_unreadable_record: live worker plus injected PermissionDenied on its run.json; a second same-task start must refuse before any launch marker.
findings.remedy: Match ErrorKind::NotFound to Ok(None) in read_record and Err on all other I/O errors; make run_dirs, live_run and other_live_run return Result; claim_for_spawn refuses on any Err.

findings.claim: Proposed remedy for F91-3: event-file read errors become artifact errors; temporary attempt files survive until their contents are durably incorporated; an unreadable aggregate stream never replaces a valid report.
findings.trigger: Reading an attempt's temp events file fails while removal still succeeds, or a transient read failure on events.jsonl during refresh_artifacts follows a successfully classified attempt.

evidence.observation: refresh_artifacts uses read_to_string(...).unwrap_or_default() for events.jsonl and writes the resulting report without surfacing a read error.

findings.verification: New test artifact_read_failure_preserves_bytes: injected read failures on the attempt and aggregate event files; expect nonzero exit, artifact_error, retained source bytes, and the prior report.md intact.
findings.remedy: Propagate events.jsonl read errors from refresh_artifacts when the file exists; read attempt temp files before append, finish artifact_error on failure, delete temp files only after a durably successful append.

findings.claim: Proposed remedy for F91-4: Claude success requires an explicitly valid result (is_error present and false, non-empty result text); Codex success requires turn.completed alone, with agent_message used only for report extraction; the unit test at engines.rs:651 codifies the bug and must be inverted.
findings.trigger: An exit-zero launcher emits {"type":"result"} with no is_error (Claude) or only an agent_message item.completed (Codex), then ends without a successful terminal.

evidence.observation: Claude maps has_result with is_error false (absent counts) to Success; Codex sets saw_completed for an agent_message item.completed as well as turn.completed.
terminal_outcome_reads_the_stream asserts Success for a Codex agent_message-only stream.

findings.verification: New test terminal_requires_affirmative_success driving both stated streams with exit code 0 through classify_attempt; require died in both cases, never done.
findings.remedy: Tighten the Claude branch to require is_error == Some(false) and a non-empty result; restrict the Codex saw_completed flag to turn.completed and keep agent_message parsing in summarize only; update the existing test expectation.

findings.claim: Scoring: credit the solver only on adopted AND verified, credit the finder only for the finding, penalize a rejected blocker against finder precision, and revoke solver credit when a verified fix resurfaces as a remaining case in the next pass.
findings.trigger: Feeding remedy outcomes into the router as a second 'solver' dimension without letting finders game it with easy blockers.

evidence.reference: brief Q4 and the pass-1/pass-2 history
evidence.observation: Adoption alone is coordinator taste; the 0.2.3 loop shows fixes that pass adoption but fail the next review, so verification is the only ground truth available.

findings.verification: Simulate the pass-1/pass-2 0.2.3 history under the proposed credit rules and confirm the wave-10a worker fixes would not have earned lasting solver credit.
findings.remedy: Store adoption and verification as separate router signals; solver score = verified/(adopted); finder precision = confirmed/(raised); resurface of the same case decrements the prior solver credit.

findings.claim: The finder/solver/verifier separation is sound, with verification by a third party plus solver-provided tests.
findings.trigger: The current acceptance loop where the same model finds and verifies fixes.

evidence.observation: Same-model verification creates frame confirmation bias, leading to repeated HOLD passes.

findings.verification: Run a trial panel with 3 blockers, measure fix rate per pass vs current loop.
findings.remedy: Use the finder to state acceptance criteria, 2-3 external solvers for remedies, and a third model for verification. Require solvers to ship a test case with each proposal. Batch blockers to reduce panel cost.

findings.claim: The minimal workflow requires manual coordinator adoption of proposals; full automation would introduce quality risks.
findings.trigger: The coordinator's sketch which includes automatic triggers for remedy panels.

evidence.observation: Proposals require tradeoffs between complexity, risk, and scope that cannot be reliably automated.

findings.verification: Audit the first 10 remedy panels to confirm adoption decisions are not trivial.
findings.remedy: The proposals record needs only proposer identity, approach, code locations, test case, and risks. Exclude the finder's vendor from remedy panels. Do NOT automate proposal adoption: require the coordinator to explicitly select or reject each proposal with a reason.

findings.claim: Moving all resume admission eligibility checks inside the admission lock eliminates stale-state resume races.
findings.trigger: The stale resume race described in F91-1.

evidence.observation: Current checks run before lock acquisition, using stale state that can change before the lock is held.

findings.verification: Run the stale_resume_barrier test; confirm no second launch marker is written.
findings.remedy: In resume_once, move allowed status and exhausted checks after claim_for_spawn. In claim_for_spawn, recheck terminal status/exhaustion on the locked record, and calculate the attempt number from that record. Reject if the pre-lock attempt number does not match the locked next attempt.

findings.claim: Propagating event read errors and deferring temporary file deletion prevents data loss on read failures.
findings.trigger: The artifact read failure cases in F91-3.

evidence.observation: Current code uses unwrap_or_default and deletes files even on read failure, leading to empty reports and lost data.

findings.verification: Run the read_failure_preservation test; confirm source bytes are retained and artifact_error is set.
findings.remedy: Remove unwrap_or_default from attempt and aggregate event reads. Return read errors from append_resume and refresh_artifacts. Delete temporary attempt files only after a successful append. Skip report writes when the source events file cannot be read.

findings.claim: Dual credit for finder (valid blocker) and solver (adopted + verified fix) prevents gaming and improves routing.
findings.trigger: The need to score solvers separately from finders in the router.

evidence.observation: Current router only scores finding usefulness, not remedy quality, so good solvers cannot be identified.

findings.verification: Track proposal adoption and verification rates for 20 panels; confirm solver scores correlate with fix success.
findings.remedy: Credit finders when their blocker is verified fixed. Credit solvers only when their proposal is both adopted and verified. Penalize finders for invalid blockers and solvers for failed proposals. Use separate solver and finder scores for routing.

findings.claim: The proposed finder/solver/verifier pipeline creates high latency, context-blind patches, and moving-goalpost failure modes without addressing the root cause: underspecified acceptance criteria.
findings.trigger: A reviewer raises a blocker with a one-sentence remedy; solvers without whole-repo context propose divergent architectures which the finder later rejects.

evidence.observation: Pass 2 raised edge cases missed by pass 1 fixes due to one-sentence remedies lacking negative test criteria.

findings.verification: Compare the acceptance pass rate of one-sentence remedies against executable test specification contracts on acceptance loops.
findings.remedy: Require finders to provide executable reproduction triggers or strict acceptance criteria contracts rather than narrative directions. Treat automated regression test execution as primary verification instead of subjective model reviews. Keep multi-model panels optional and budget-capped.

findings.claim: Resume admission permits stale state reuse because status checks, quota exhaustion, and attempt calculation occur before acquiring the admission lock.
findings.trigger: Concurrent or delayed resume after a run has transitioned to terminal status or exhausted quota.

evidence.observation: claim_for_spawn accepts precomputed attempt number and only checks other live runs and current pid, ignoring terminal status and exhaustion.
Attempt counter n is calculated before acquiring the admission lock in resume_once.
do_resume_foreground checks status and exhaustion before calling resume_once without locking.

findings.verification: Run RC1: inject a barrier prior to claim_for_spawn while another process transitions the record to done or exhausted; confirm delayed command is rejected.
findings.remedy: Move status validation, quota exhaustion check, and calculation of attempt = quota.resumes + 1 inside claim_for_spawn under record::admission_lock. Reject any claim where status is not quota or timeout or where quota is exhausted. Return the updated RunRecord and attempt number to resume_once, eliminating stale pre-lock calculations.

findings.claim: Admission lock fails open when candidate run records or directories encounter I/O or permission errors, treating unreadable runs as non-existent.
findings.trigger: A candidate run record cannot be read due to permission denial or I/O failure while another worker is active.

evidence.observation: read_record maps all std::fs::read errors unconditionally to Ok(None).
run_dirs returns an empty list on read_dir errors and ignores unreadable entries.
other_live_run silently flattens record read errors to None, assuming no run is live.

findings.verification: Run RC2: inject PermissionDenied on a candidate run.json; verify claim_for_spawn refuses admission with an explicit error rather than spawning.
findings.remedy: Differentiate ErrorKind::NotFound from other I/O errors in read_record, returning Ok(None) solely when the file is genuinely absent. Propagate inspection errors through run_dirs, live_run, and other_live_run. Enforce fail-closed admission in claim_for_spawn by aborting if any candidate run record cannot be inspected.

findings.claim: Crediting solvers on proposal adoption incentivizes shallow, crowd-pleasing patches and allows finders to game scores by raising trivial blockers.
findings.trigger: Routing updates driven by coordinator adoption marks before downstream verification.

evidence.observation: Proposal states coordinator marks adopted feed the router as a solver dimension.

findings.verification: Track whether adopted proposals that fail subsequent verification inflate solver routing weights.
findings.remedy: Decouple proposal adoption from router scoring. Award solver credit only after verified clean runs, penalize regressions, and track finder precision independently to prevent blocker inflation.

findings.claim: Do not build the full remedy panel yet; run a single-solver spike on the two F91 blockers first because the brief's framing assumes the miss is finder taste rather than an underspecified remedy contract.
findings.trigger: Coordinator accepts the vendor-diversity panel as the only fix for the fix-missed-case loop.

evidence.observation: Pass 2 text says 2 of 4 findings are 'remaining case' of pass-1 blockers and remedy is one sentence direction, worker makes design choices alone.
F91-1 stale-claim, F91-2 fail-open on unreadable records, F91-3 destructive read-default, F91-4 weak terminal detector all cite locked reread / default-on-error paths.

findings.verification: Compare next-pass remaining-case rate with tightened remedy text versus full 3-solver panel on the same two blockers.
findings.remedy: Before any new purpose or router dimension, require structured remedy plus finder acceptance criteria in the existing schema, run one solver on F91-1/F91-2, and only generalize if the remaining-case rate drops. Alternatives the brief omits: richer remedy field alone, coordinator-generated worker brief from finding, single solver not panel of 3, rule-fix without panel, or pausing c3 work acceptance.

findings.claim: Finder/solver split is sound but verifier should be the solver-shipped failing test re-run by the coordinator plus finder re-inspection, not a third member by default.
findings.trigger: A blocker enters remedy; solver lacks repo access or finder rejects every foreign fix.

evidence.observation: Sketch assigns verifier as finder or third member; finder already costs ~280s and 9-16% window per pass with 40-60min worker wave between.
Three consultations per blocker triples window cost and adds finder-rejects-foreign-fix and solver-without-codebase failure modes.

findings.verification: RC1-RC3 in handoff 91 pass without extra consultation: barrier resume refused, denied-read refused, bad terminal streams yield died not done.
findings.remedy: Finder states machine-checkable acceptance criteria; solver must ship patch sketch plus failing-then-passing test; coordinator runs test, finder confirms trigger closed on next pass. Use a third verifier only on solver-finder disagreement or when finder history shows high reject rate.

findings.claim: Minimal remedy record is findings[].proposals[] with proposer identity, approach, code locations, patch sketch, test, risks, confidence, plus coordinator decision adopted/rejected with reason; fit it in files-are-the-record without new automation.
findings.trigger: HOLD with blockers where coordinator wants competing fixes under ledger.

evidence.observation: Bridge already has findings[].remedy, prior_findings per-id status, roles by score rank with Kuhn matching, pack builder, and c3 work worker.
Pack of located code plus existing tests is lossy for TOCTOU and permission paths unless denial fixtures are included.

findings.verification: Inspect findings.json: proposals stored under finding id with identity, exactly one adopted with reason, no auto-run on HOLD.
findings.remedy: Add purpose remedy reusing consult reply schema, roles solver-for-F-id, pack must include located code plus failing fixtures and record/attempt fixtures. Coordinator records adopted/rejected with reason in findings.json. Must NOT automate: auto-trigger on HOLD, auto-pick by confidence, auto-implement without coordinator choice, or solver-score writes without verified fix.

findings.claim: F91-1 remedy: move all admission validation inside the admission lock in claim_for_spawn/resume_once and derive the attempt number from the same locked record with generation check.
findings.trigger: Two resumes race; second resumes after first reached done or exhausted=true with stale n.

evidence.observation: F91-1: status/exhaustion checked before lock, attempt n calculated before lock, locked reread checks only live owner then sets running unconditionally.
Module owns guards and run via record/detach lifecycle; record written by c3 never worker.

findings.verification: Test work_resume_stale_claim_refused: barrier before second claim_for_spawn, first reaches done and separately exhausted, require delayed claim refuses with no launch marker.
findings.remedy: Under admission_lock, reread RunRecord, reject if terminal or exhausted or owner mismatch or caller attempt != locked attempts.len()+1, compute n from locked record, then mark running atomically. Stale caller gets refusal before any child-launch marker. Invariant: at most one running attempt per task and attempt numbers are dense and monotonic.

findings.claim: F91-2 remedy: make admission fail-closed on inspection errors through read_record, run_dirs, live_run, and other_live_run.
findings.trigger: Live worker holds run.json that a second starter cannot read, or enumeration/entry error occurs.

evidence.observation: F91-2: every fs::read error returns Ok(None) including access failures; run_dirs empty on enum failure, flattens entry errors, live_run and other_live_run discard read/parse errors.
Exact error-enum signatures in record.rs not re-read under 6-call budget; shape follows F91-2 locations.

findings.verification: Test work_admission_denied_read_refuses: live blocking worker plus read-deny on its run.json, require second start/resume refuses before launch.
findings.remedy: Return Result with typed InspectionError; treat only confirmed NotFound as absence; any denied/parse/enumeration error refuses admission before launch with a distinct message. Invariant: admission proceeds only from fully inspected state; unknown means refuse. Add read-deny fixture using OS ACL or injected PermissionDenied.

findings.claim: Credit solver only on verified fix and credit finder only on surviving blockers, with separate router dimensions and anti-gaming guards.
findings.trigger: Adopted proposal merged or finder raises low-severity blockers to farm solver closes.

evidence.observation: Sketch proposes adoption marks feed router as second solver dimension alongside finder ratings useful yes/partly/no keyed by consult_id.
Adoption alone rewards persuasive sketches; finder can inflate score by raising easy blockers that solvers fix trivially.

findings.verification: Router query shows solver and finder dimensions diverge for a member with one lucky adopt versus repeated verified closes.
findings.remedy: Solver gets solver-point only when its adopted proposal passes RC test and finder closes finding on next pass; partial credit if merged. Finder gets finder-point only if blocker survives worker fix to next pass or is rated useful, decayed if overturned as non-blocker. Keep finder and solver scores as separate router keys; require at least two verified closes before routing weight.

findings.claim: Pilot an invariant-driven workflow with one solver and conditional independent review; the reported acceptance loop does not establish that separating finder and solver identities will reduce recurrence.
findings.trigger: Repeated acceptance failures lead to a proposal for multiple remedy consultations per blocker.

evidence.observation: The brief describes two acceptance passes, implementation between them, and substantial consultation and worker costs; it provides no comparison of alternative workflows.
The observed gaps concern transition preconditions and incomplete error propagation, both of which require explicit invariant coverage regardless of solver identity.

findings.verification: Compare a bounded set of similar repairs using one solver plus explicit invariant tests against independent alternatives, recording total closure time, reviewer cost and reopened defects.
findings.remedy: Start with a reproducer and acceptance criteria, then assign one solver per related invariant cluster; allow the finder to contribute a design without making it authoritative. The finder checks the original trigger, the coordinator assesses the patch and regressions, and a third reviewer resolves criterion disputes or substantial residual risk. Require rejection to identify a counterexample or violated criterion, and select panel size using repository familiarity, context completeness, recurrence causes and measured closure cost.

findings.claim: Proposal provenance and selection history must remain separate from finding status and verification evidence.
findings.trigger: A coordinator adopts, combines, revises or declines competing proposals, potentially against different code revisions.

evidence.observation: Finding stores source, status history and reviewer checks; unknown members survive rewrites through extra, and set_status binds transitions to history events.
The design makes files authoritative and keeps reviewer execution read-only.

findings.verification: Round-trip a finding containing two proposals and a merged decision through existing finding operations; require preserved provenance, append-only decision history and unchanged finding status until an explicit supported transition.
findings.remedy: Record proposal ID, finding IDs, consult ID, reviewer identity, code/finding/pack digests, approach, locations, patch sketch, invariant, test specification, assumptions and risks, with immutable reply references. Append decisions recording actor, timestamp, selected IDs and rationale; give merged designs a new ID with parent links and attach the eventual implementation revision. Distinguish not_selected from technically rejected, and keep adoption independent of implemented or verified finding status.

findings.claim: A solver needs invariant-relevant context and explicit eligibility rules; cited code alone and blanket vendor exclusion are insufficient selection criteria.
findings.trigger: A repository-unfamiliar reviewer receives a generated pack, or excluding the finder's vendor removes the available qualified solver.

evidence.observation: The sketch proposes packs from finding locations and existing tests, exclusion of the finder's vendor, and automatic preparation of a remedy command.
The alarm has an owner-preserving waiting state, and a nominal record reader performs recovery writes; these affect a correct admission remedy beyond the original locked claim.

findings.verification: Review a generated F91-1 pack against an explicit dependency checklist and inspect its proposed roster when an exclusion leaves insufficient eligible solvers.
findings.remedy: Pilot an existing solver role before adding a remedy purpose, supplying callers, writers, state definitions, liveness/locking dependencies, error paths, tests and disclosed omissions in the pack. Prefer qualified independent laboratories while preserving explicit coordinator-provider exclusions and never silently relaxing constraints. Automate preparation and validation, but leave consultation spending, proposal selection/merging, worker execution and verification decisions with the coordinator.

findings.claim: For F91-1, replace unconditional resume claiming with a locked, intent-specific state transition that rejects stale snapshots and reserves a fresh attempt.
findings.trigger: A delayed resume reaches claim_for_spawn after another resume has completed, exhausted the cap, or advanced to a later resumable attempt.

evidence.observation: State and exhaustion checks and attempt calculation occur before the lock; the locked path rejects a different live PID but otherwise writes running with the supplied attempt.
The alarm parks the record as waiting_quota while retaining ownership and later calls resume_once, so a foreground-only allowed-state rule would break this path.
read_record can write a recovered died state without itself acquiring admission_lock.

findings.verification: Run RC1: resume_claim_rejects_stale_snapshot must reject delayed claims after done, exhausted quota and a later resumable generation without another launch marker, while a valid alarm claim succeeds.
findings.remedy: Pass explicit foreground/alarm intent and an expected attempt/state snapshot through do_resume_foreground, run_alarm and resume_once into claim_for_spawn. Under admission_lock, reread and validate the expected snapshot, allowed state, exhaustion, effective resume cap and owner identity including process start, then reserve and return the next attempt from that record. Permit waiting_quota only for its matching alarm owner; never exempt arbitrary running states merely because the PID matches. Split pure record reading from recovery mutation and serialize recovery transitions with admission so a stale recovery writer cannot undo a fresh claim.

findings.claim: For F91-2, make the entire admission inspection chain fallible, including metadata filtering, so unreadable competing records cannot be interpreted as absent workers.
findings.trigger: A live worker's record or directory cannot be inspected while another command can acquire the task admission lock.

evidence.observation: read_record maps every read failure to absence; run_dirs suppresses enumeration and entry errors and filters through is_file; both live-run functions discard record errors.
Allocation and admission depend on these scans, so changing only the record reader would leave other paths treating uncertainty as absence.

findings.verification: Run RC2: admission_fails_closed_on_inspection_error must refuse before allocation or launch for read, metadata, enumeration, entry and parse failures; confirmed absence and readable terminal records must retain their intended behavior.
findings.remedy: Return Result from run_dirs, live_run and other_live_run and propagate failures through allocate and all admission callers. In read_record, treat only confirmed NotFound as absence and retain path-specific errors otherwise; replace is_file with fallible metadata inspection and do not flatten directory-entry failures. Preserve the invariant that a claim is admitted only after competing candidate records are inspectable, while keeping diagnostic listing failures explicit rather than silently returning an empty list.

findings.claim: Use verified contribution outcomes for solver routing; adoption alone measures coordinator preference and cannot establish remedy quality.
findings.trigger: The router credits selected proposals before implementation succeeds, penalizes viable unselected alternatives, or rewards finders for generating many easy blockers.

evidence.observation: The sketch feeds adoption marks into a new solver score dimension.
The documented router uses consultation usefulness ratings, treats missing ratings as missing rather than zero, and applies a prior-smoothed weighting formula.
Selection occurs before verified implementation and is affected by coordinator preferences and resource limits; unselected proposals lack observed implementation outcomes.

findings.verification: Replay synthetic outcomes containing an adopted-but-failed proposal, an unselected viable proposal, a verified merged fix and duplicate findings; require no correctness credit from adoption alone and no failure credit for unobserved alternatives.
findings.remedy: Keep adoption as a descriptive signal and award solver correctness credit only for a linked, verified implementation, recording material worker changes and merged contributions. Credit finders for independently substantiated, deduplicated defects rather than severity labels, finding counts or downstream adoption, and record verifier quality separately. Treat unimplemented alternatives as missing outcomes, retain sample counts and conservative priors with exploration, and evaluate closure cost and reopen rate alongside correctness.

findings.claim: The verifier role should be the solver's shipped test plus the finder's pre-committed acceptance criteria, adjudicated by the finder on its next acceptance pass; a third consultation member adds window cost without new information.
findings.trigger: A blocker is raised and one or more remedies proposed; someone must decide who confirms the fix closes the finding.

evidence.observation: The finder's pass already adjudicates prior_findings[] with per-id status (fixed/still-open) and lists first_run_checklist evidence - the verification vehicle exists and is already paid for.
Each split is a case the finder knew but never stated as closing evidence, so verification-by-criteria was never possible for the worker.

findings.verification: Run one acceptance loop where the finder writes acceptance[] before the worker acts; confirm the next pass closes the findings in a single wave.
findings.remedy: Add an acceptance[] field (test name + what it drives, or the exact observable refusal) to the finding record, written by the finder before proposals are shown. The solver's test is run by the worker; the finder's next pass adjudicates only against the committed criteria. Do not seat a third verifier member.

findings.claim: A default three-seat remedy panel per blocker is too expensive: at 9-16 % of the reviewer's 5-hour window per consultation plus a worker wave, two blockers can consume over half the window per pass; the panel should be an escalation, not the default path.
findings.trigger: Any HOLD with two or more blockers (the current situation: F91-1 and F91-2 are both blockers).

evidence.observation: Cost today: ~280 s and 9-16 % of Astra's 5-hour window per pass; a worker wave of 40-60 minutes between passes.
3 seats x 2 blockers x ~9-16 % window share, plus two worker waves, exceeds the current loop cost it is meant to reduce.

findings.verification: Measure the wall-clock and window share of one escalated panel (a repeat-failure finding) against one criteria-only loop; the panel must reduce total passes-to-close, not just per-pass quality.
findings.remedy: Convene the multi-seat panel only when a finding supersedes a prior one (repeat failure, i.e. the worker's design was narrow) or when criteria conflict; otherwise run a single solver seat. Offer the exact --remedy line on HOLD as sketched, but never run it automatically.

findings.claim: The minimal ledger extension is findings[].acceptance[] (finder, committed before proposals are visible) plus findings[].proposals[] {proposer, approach, locations, patch_sketch, test{name, drives}, risks, confidence}, with lifecycle proposed -> adopted|rejected(reason) -> verified|failed recorded by the finder's next pass.
findings.trigger: The remedy purpose runs; its outputs must land somewhere in the files-are-the-record ledger without a new store.

evidence.observation: The ingested reply schema already carries findings[].remedy, prior_findings[].status and evidence blocks; proposals[] and acceptance[] are additive fields of the same shape.

evidence.reference: Brief: crates/c3/src/consult/ ingests the schema; c3 findings sets status
evidence.observation: A new enum transition (proposed/adopted) fits the existing status mechanism; not independently read.

findings.verification: Ingest one real remedy reply into findings.json and confirm `c3 findings` displays acceptance[], proposals[] with proposer identity, and the adopted/rejected states.
findings.remedy: Store proposals under the finding id with the proposer's identity and consult_id; the coordinator records adopted/rejected plus a reason as a plain status transition. Never automate the adoption choice, the finder's criteria, worker execution, or the verified mark; test-green alone must not set verified.

findings.claim: A solver seat without repository read access will propose patches that do not compile across callers: the F91-2 remedy alone changes the signatures of run_dirs/live_run/other_live_run, and the pack must therefore include every caller (e.g. run() at mod.rs:904), not just the located lines.
findings.trigger: The coordinator seats a pack-fed http-engine model as a solver for a finding whose remedy spans module boundaries.

evidence.observation: run_dirs, live_run and other_live_run are pub helpers consumed by admission paths in mod.rs (run() at 904, claim_for_spawn at 749) - changing their return type is a cross-file change.

evidence.reference: Brief: pack/ builds a token-budgeted context for models that cannot read the repository
evidence.observation: A pack generated from the finding's locations alone would omit callers; pack composition is the mitigation, not read.

findings.verification: Ask a pack-fed solver for an F91-2 proposal and check whether it mentions updating run(); if not, restrict solver seats to repo-reading engines or fix the pack template.
findings.remedy: Prefer repo-reading engines (claude, codex) for solver seats; when a pack-fed model must serve, generate the pack from the located functions plus their callers and the existing tests, and require every proposal to name exact functions and a test that compiles before the coordinator may adopt it.

findings.claim: Remedy for F91-1: all resume eligibility (permitted prior status, exhaustion) and the attempt number must be derived inside claim_for_spawn from the reread taken under the admission lock; today resume_once computes n from a pre-lock read and the claim's is_pending guard lets a terminal record be overwritten running with a stale attempt.
findings.trigger: Two resumes pass the unlocked checks; the second parks before claim_for_spawn; the first finishes done or exhausts the cap; the second's locked claim sees a terminal record, passes the live-owner check, and relaunches.

evidence.observation: resume_once reads the record and computes n = quota.resumes + 1 before taking the admission lock in claim_for_spawn.

claim_for_spawn checks only other_live_run and a live different owner (is_pending && is_live && pid mismatch); a done record fails is_pending, skips the refusal, and is unconditionally written running with the passed-in attempt.
The status/exhaustion pre-checks live around mod.rs:1386 (not read in this consultation's budget); the finder observed they operate on the pre-lock record.

findings.verification: Run RC1-style barrier test resume_refuses_when_record_became_terminal_between_read_and_claim: the delayed resume must refuse and run.json must show no second child-launch marker or attempt bump.
findings.remedy: Give claim_for_spawn the set of permitted prior statuses and have it compute n itself from the locked reread, refusing terminal or quota-exhausted records; keep the unlocked checks only as fast refusals. Invariant: the status, owner and attempt written under the admission lock derive solely from state read under that same lock. Test drives two resumes with a barrier between the second's eligibility check and its claim, letting the first reach done and separately exhausted=true.

findings.claim: Remedy for F91-2: read_record must return Ok(None) only on confirmed NotFound and Err otherwise, and run_dirs/live_run/other_live_run must propagate inspection errors so admission refuses when any candidate record cannot be inspected; today every read error, enumeration failure and parse error is treated as absence.
findings.trigger: A worker is live while another process can take the admission lock but cannot read that worker's run.json (or hits a directory-enumeration or entry error); a second start or resume skips the live run.

evidence.observation: read_record maps every std::fs::read error to Ok(None); only a parse failure of read bytes becomes Err.
run_dirs returns an empty Vec on read_dir error and flattens entry errors; live_run and other_live_run discard read/parse errors via .ok().flatten() before the is_pending/is_live filter.

findings.verification: Run admission_refuses_when_live_record_unreadable: a live blocking worker plus an injected PermissionDenied (or denied handle) on its run.json; a second same-task command must refuse before any launch.
findings.remedy: Match on ErrorKind::NotFound for absence and propagate every other error through run_dirs (Result), read_record, live_run and other_live_run (Result<Option<_>>), making the admission callers in run() and claim_for_spawn refuse on uninspectable candidates. Invariant: the no-live-run conclusion requires positive inspection of every candidate record, never an assumed absence. Update the callers in mod.rs (904, 749) in the same change.

findings.claim: Remedy for F91-3: event-file read failures must propagate as artifact_error and temporary attempt files must survive until their bytes are read and durably appended; today an unreadable tmp stream becomes an empty string, append_resume successfully appends nothing, and both tmp files are then deleted; refresh_artifacts likewise defaults an unreadable events.jsonl to an empty report.
findings.trigger: A resumed child writes a valid successful stream, but reading .events-resume-N.jsonl (or events.jsonl during refresh) fails transiently while deletion remains possible; the attempt is lost yet the run can still be recorded done.

evidence.observation: attempt_events/attempt_stderr use unwrap_or_default; append_resume is then called with the (possibly empty) text and only after its success are both tmp files removed.
refresh_artifacts reads events.jsonl with unwrap_or_default and writes the resulting report without any read error; the caller then applies the earlier classified status including done.

findings.verification: Inject read failures separately on the attempt tmp file and on events.jsonl; require retained source bytes on disk, status artifact_error, and a nonzero exit in both cases.
findings.remedy: Replace unwrap_or_default at mod.rs:858 and mod.rs:1175-1176 with propagated errors routed to finish_artifact_error, and delete tmp attempt files only after their contents were read and the append flushed. Invariant: an artifact is never replaced or dropped on the basis of a read failure; unread source bytes stay on disk. Test artifact_read_failure_preserves_attempt_bytes drives a valid attempt with an injected read error on the tmp file.

findings.claim: Remedy for F91-4: done must require affirmative successful terminal evidence - the Claude arm of terminal_outcome must require an explicit is_error:false on the result (absent is_error currently defaults to success), and the Codex arm must not treat an item.completed agent_message as completion; success is turn.completed only.
findings.trigger: An exit-zero launcher emits only {"type":"result"} for Claude, or only an item.completed agent_message item for Codex, then ends; the run is classified done without a successful turn terminal.

evidence.observation: Claude maps has_result && !is_error to Success; the Codex arm sets saw_completed for item.completed with an agent_message item exactly as for turn.completed.

Finder's evidence: record.rs:544-551 sets is_error false unless the field is exactly boolean true (absent included), and the unit at engines.rs:636-655 asserts Success for an agent_message-only stream.
The is_error default was taken from the finder's citation; that region was not read within this consultation's tool budget.

findings.verification: Run exit_zero_without_affirmative_terminal_is_not_done with the two stated streams and process exit zero; require died (missing terminal evidence), never done; the existing agent_message-only unit expectation must be flipped in the same change.
findings.remedy: In the Claude arm require the summarized result to carry is_error explicitly false, mapping an absent field to Terminal::None; delete the agent_message branch in the Codex arm (engines.rs:504-512) so only turn.completed sets completion, keeping assistant-message extraction separate from classification. Invariant: classify_attempt's done requires exit 0 plus the engine's own affirmative success terminal.

findings.claim: Scoring: credit the solver only when the fix is verified (adoption alone pays nothing), keep finder and solver as separate non-zero-sum dimensions, discount supersedes-chains so a finder cannot farm credit by splitting its own finding, and defer the router's solver dimension until roughly ten verified proposals exist.
findings.trigger: The coordinator begins marking proposals adopted/rejected and findings verified; the router needs a signal that cannot be gamed by a finder raising easy blockers or self-splitting findings.

evidence.observation: This single reply already contains three supersedes chains (F89-2, F89-3, F89-8) - the self-split pattern the scoring must discount is the norm, not an edge case.

evidence.reference: Brief: panel.routing, ratings useful yes|partly|no keyed by consult_id
evidence.observation: The existing usefulness rating already gives the coordinator an independent per-consultation finder signal; internals not read.

findings.verification: After the first five adoptions, check that a rejected-but-implemented proposal and an adopted-but-unverified one carry no solver credit, and that a superseding finding credited its finder only once.
findings.remedy: Record adoption and verification events per proposal now (the data is cheap), but compute no solver score until ~10 verified samples exist; finder credit accrues per distinct finding with supersedes chains credited once at the delta, moderated by the coordinator's existing useful rating. This keeps early vendor diversity from being flattened by coordinator taste in adoptions.

findings.claim: The remedy-panel proposal rests on a diagnosis the acceptance record contradicts. The pass-1 to pass-2 pattern (8 findings fixed, 4 returned, two of them 'the remaining case' of the same blockers) is evidence of under-specified invariants and absent regression tests, not of the finder confirming its own frame. Adding design alternatives does not produce the artifact that closes the loop: a test that fails before the fix and passes after.
findings.trigger: Any blocker whose remedy is a one-sentence direction, implemented by a worker that makes the design choices alone.

evidence.observation: Both carry supersedes: [F89-2] and [F89-8] with prose like 'the lock closes the straightforward simultaneous-live resume race, but the admission claim remains stale-state susceptible' - the previous remedy was followed, the invariant was not stated.
The invariant the fix must establish exists today only as a prose doc comment; nothing in the code or tests asserts it.

findings.verification: Classify the 12 findings of passes 1-2 by cause (invariant unstated / test absent / design contested) and check whether the two 'remaining case' findings would have been caught by a test derived from the pass-1 trigger. If most are invariant-unstated, the panel is not the first intervention.
findings.remedy: Make the finding's own artifact the acceptance criterion before any design work: require findings[].test {name, drives, fails_before} alongside remedy, where fails_before names the observed pre-fix result. Treat the test, not the finder's opinion, as the verifier of record. Build the remedy panel as the second intervention, scoped to findings whose cause is a contested design (e.g. the error-propagation API shape in F91-2), not to every blocker.

findings.claim: The brief lists only one option (a cross-lab solver panel) for a problem with at least four cheaper alternatives, and no option for the case where no proposal is adoptable.
findings.trigger: Any HOLD with blockers, where the coordinator must decide how to spend the window.

evidence.observation: The proposal and its rationale are stated; no alternative intervention and no 'no proposal adopted' outcome appear anywhere in the brief.
F91-3 is an ordering defect (read source, then delete it; append before refresh) with a singular correct design - a design panel has nothing to choose between.

findings.verification: For each of F91-1..F91-4, write down the number of genuinely distinct designs; if any is 1, that finding must not be sent to a panel.
findings.remedy: Add these options to the decision list: (a) blank-slate re-design by the finder with its own remedy text withheld (removes frame-confirmation at zero vendor cost); (b) a second lab reviewing the implemented diff rather than designing from a pack (cheaper input, targets the missed case); (c) a one-time deterministic schedule/state harness for the read-state-then-act family F91-1/2/3; (d) a no-panel fast path for singular-design fixes; (e) an explicit 'no proposal adopted - the finder's remedy stands / escalate to the operator' outcome, without which a panel always yields a fix and launders the decision.

findings.claim: The cost model in the brief is the wrong axis. Window percentage, not wall-clock seconds, is the scarce resource: N parallel solvers consume N x 280 s of window for one pass's wall-clock, so the panel does not save the 40-60 minute worker wave and multiplies the constraint that actually binds.
findings.trigger: A HOLD with several blockers; the coordinator offers one --remedy line per blocker.

evidence.observation: The brief records 280 s and 9-16% of a 5-hour window per pass and a 40-60 minute worker wave between passes, then proposes three consultations per blocker.
Pass 2 raised 4 findings at once; F91-1 and F91-2 are one admission-lock problem reported as two, so per-blocker panels would brief the same code twice.

findings.verification: Sum the window percentage of the last three acceptance passes and compare it with the proposed three-consultation panel on the same findings.
findings.remedy: Budget the panel in window percent and pre-commit it before the first solver call. Brief per finding family (F91-1+F91-2 are one admission brief), cap at two solvers, and require the coordinator to state the window it is willing to spend before the panel starts. Parallelism reduces wall-clock only, so never justify the panel by the worker wave.

findings.claim: --exclude-vendor <finder's lab> can leave one or zero eligible solvers, and vendor diversity is not solver independence: models sharing training data and a shared brief produce correlated proposals, so 'one reviewer's taste becomes a decision between alternatives' is an assumption, not a property.
findings.trigger: A roster with few labs, or a panel where every eligible member proposes the same approach.
