evidence.reference: roster composition (README.md 'Reviewer roster and panel', not read in this consultation)
evidence.observation: Not checked: how many distinct labs the roster holds, so the number of solvers surviving an exclude-vendor filter is unknown.
Panels seat by willingness via Kuhn matching on score rank; nothing in the described mechanism guarantees a minimum number of eligible solvers after exclusion.

findings.verification: Run RC5: send the F91-1 brief to two labs and diff the approach fields. Identical approaches settle the correlation question against the panel's rationale.
findings.remedy: Require at least two eligible solvers after exclusion; otherwise skip the panel and record the skip and its reason in sessions.json rather than running a one-member panel that produces a single taste with panel provenance. Measure divergence on a replay before building the feature, and if proposals correlate, prefer option (b) - an independent diff review - which does not depend on the diversity assumption.

findings.claim: F91-1 remedy: make the admission lock the only place the spawn decision is made. claim_for_spawn takes a ClaimExpectation {allowed_statuses, expected_attempt, require_not_exhausted}; resume_once stops computing n before the lock and passes the generation it read; claim_for_spawn re-reads under the lock, computes n = quota.resumes + 1 from that same read, and refuses on terminal status, exhausted quota, a live foreign owner, or a generation mismatch. The pre-lock checks stay only as fast-fail UX and are explicitly non-authoritative.
findings.trigger: Two resumes pass the quota/non-exhausted checks; the second pauses before claim_for_spawn while the first reaches done or exhausts the cap.

evidence.observation: n is computed from a pre-lock read_record, then claim_for_spawn is called with that n as a parameter - the lock never sees the state n was derived from.

Under the lock the code checks other_live_run and a foreign live owner, then unconditionally sets status=running, pid, attempt=attempt and writes; terminal status, exhaustion and the attempt generation are not re-checked.

findings.verification: Test crates/c3/tests/work_admission.rs::stale_resume_claim_is_refused - drive it with a test-only barrier hook injected between the pre-lock read and the lock acquisition: let the first resume reach done (case A) and then quota with exhausted=true (case B); require Err and no status write in both.
findings.remedy: Change the signature to claim_for_spawn(work_root, rec_dir, expect: ClaimExpectation) -> Result<RunRecord, String>, compute the attempt number inside it from the locked read, and expose a #[cfg(test)] before_claim hook so the interleaving is deterministic. Invariant: every transition into running is decided from record state read under the admission lock, and the attempt number is a function of that same read.

findings.claim: F91-2 remedy: distinguish confirmed absence from failed inspection, and fail closed. Add read_record_strict returning Err for any error other than ErrorKind::NotFound and for parse failures; run_dirs returns Result and propagates read_dir and entry errors instead of flattening them; other_live_run and live_run return Result and propagate; claim_for_spawn refuses admission with the failing record named when any candidate cannot be inspected. Keep the lenient read_record for display paths (--status, --wait) so the blast radius stays inside admission.
findings.trigger: A live worker holds a record that a second process can allocate a directory beside but cannot read (PermissionDenied, sharing violation), or an enumeration/entry error occurs.

evidence.observation: std::fs::read error is mapped to Ok(None) for every ErrorKind, including access failures - only parse errors produce Err.

run_dirs returns an empty Vec on read_dir failure and uses rd.flatten() (entry errors dropped); live_run and other_live_run call read_record(&dir).ok().flatten(), so even the parse error read_record does produce is discarded before the liveness decision.
claim_for_spawn relies on other_live_run and a single read_record; a swallowed error at either point makes it proceed to write running.

findings.verification: Test crates/c3/tests/work_admission.rs::unreadable_record_refuses_admission - create a live run directory, deny reads on its run.json (Windows share_mode(0) handle from a test helper; chmod 000 on Unix) and separately write unparseable bytes; require a refusal naming the unreadable record and no new launch marker in both cases.
findings.remedy: Introduce the strict/lenient split rather than changing read_record in place, because read_record has many display callers (see RC2). Invariant: absence of a run is asserted only on confirmed NotFound; any unreadable or unparseable candidate record makes admission refuse. A directory that exists but cannot be inspected is never evidence that no run is live.

findings.claim: F91-3 remedy: make a read failure precede and prevent the destructive step. In resume_once, match on the read of tmp_events and tmp_stderr; on Err, call finish_artifact_error and return before append_resume and before the remove_file calls, so the per-attempt bytes survive. In refresh_artifacts, propagate the events.jsonl read error (and the read_record error at line 868) as Err so the caller records artifact_error without writing report.md; write report.md only after its source read has succeeded.
findings.trigger: A resumed child writes a valid successful stream, then reading its temporary events file fails while removal would still succeed, or reading events.jsonl in refresh_artifacts fails transiently.

evidence.observation: attempt_events uses unwrap_or_default, so a failed read yields an empty string; append_resume then succeeds appending nothing, and lines 1192-1193 remove both temporary files - the bytes are gone.

events.jsonl is read with unwrap_or_default and the resulting (empty) report is written unconditionally; only the writes are error-checked, not the read. Line 868 additionally defaults a failed read_record to RunRecord::default(), silently dropping prior summary fields.
On a successful refresh the record takes the status classified earlier from the attempt stream, including done, so an empty report can be recorded done.

findings.verification: Test crates/c3/tests/work_artifacts.rs::artifact_read_failure_preserves_bytes - inject a read fault separately at the attempt-events site and the aggregate-events site; require status artifact_error, nonzero exit, .events-resume-N.jsonl still present with its original bytes, and report.md byte-identical to its pre-run content.
findings.remedy: Reorder so no source is deleted or replaced before its read succeeded: read, verify, append durably, only then remove. Invariant: an artifact is replaced only from a source that was successfully read, and a failed read is artifact_error with a nonzero exit and retained source bytes. This is a singular design - do not send it to a design panel.

findings.claim: F91-4 remedy: require affirmative, engine-specific success evidence and separate it from assistant-text extraction. Claude: treat a result as success only when is_error is present and false (or the result carries an explicit success subtype); a result missing the field is Terminal::None, not Success. Codex: delete the item.completed + agent_message arm from the success detector so only turn.completed sets saw_completed; agent_message remains in the report extractor.
findings.trigger: An exit-zero launcher emits only {"type":"result"} for Claude, or only an item.completed agent_message for Codex, then ends without a successful turn terminal.

evidence.observation: Claude returns Success whenever has_result is set and is_error is not set; Codex sets saw_completed for an item.completed agent_message as well as turn.completed, then returns Success on saw_completed alone.
The existing unit test encodes the defect as expected behaviour for the agent_message-only stream, so the test must be inverted, not merely extended.
classify_attempt maps Terminal::Success plus exit 0 to done, so an incomplete stream is recorded as a completed worker run.

findings.verification: Extend crates/c3/src/work/engines.rs::terminal_outcome_reads_the_stream with the two stated streams: require Terminal::None for each, and require Success for a Codex stream containing turn.completed and for a Claude result with is_error present and false. Then require died, not done, through classify_attempt at exit 0.
findings.remedy: Invariant: success requires an affirmative engine-specific success terminal; assistant text is never completion evidence. Keep the two concerns in separate functions so the report extractor can keep reading agent_message without conferring completion. This is a small, mechanical fix - pair it with the regression test rather than a solver panel.

findings.claim: Q1 recommendation: the finder must not verify. It should be a challenger whose acceptance criteria are frozen on record before proposals land, and the verifier of record should be the solver's test, rejected if it passes before the fix; a third member verifies only judgement calls (severity, design), never mechanical invariants.
findings.trigger: A blocker whose fix lands; the panel decides who signs it off.

evidence.observation: Every verification field is a prospective instruction to run a fixture the finder designed (RC1-RC3 in its own reply); the finder is already specifying the proof, so its later verdict tests only that the proof was run, not that the fix generalises.
A standing finder that both designs the acceptance fixture and signs the fix has an effective veto over foreign designs; 'the coordinator picks' then collapses to 'the finder approves'.

findings.verification: On the next blocker, record the finder's acceptance criteria before the proposals are read; if the finder adds a criterion after seeing a proposal, the process is not controlling the frame.
findings.remedy: Freeze findings[].verification at raise time and forbid amendments once proposals exist. The solver ships the test; the coordinator requires it to fail against the pre-fix tree (fails_before recorded). The finder's next pass is a search for the uncovered case, not a sign-off. Reserve third-member verification for contested severity or design, where no test can adjudicate.

findings.claim: Q2 recommendation: proposals live in the finding, not a new store: findings[].proposals[] = {id, consult_id, proposer{provider,model,role}, approach, locations[], patch_sketch, test{name, drives, fails_before}, pack_digest, risks, confidence, decision{value, reason, decided_by, at}}. c3 findings set <id> --adopt <proposal-id> --reason is the single writer of decision and refuses without test.fails_before. pack_digest records what the solver actually saw.
findings.trigger: A remedy consultation is run for one or more finding ids and the coordinator must record a choice.

evidence.observation: The brief states the reply schema already carries findings[].remedy and prior_findings[].status with the proposed|implemented|verified|rejected lifecycle, and that c3 findings lists and sets status - so proposals extend an existing per-finding record rather than needing a new ledger.
Not read in this consultation: whether the reply schema already has a proposals field, so RC3 is needed to decide between a schema change and a store/CLI change only.

findings.verification: Run RC3 and RC4: they settle whether proposals need a schema addition and whether a per-seat brief ('you are a solver for F91-1') is expressible with the existing --role/--roles plumbing.
findings.remedy: Record exclusion of the finder's vendor and the panel's composition in sessions.json so a one-member or degenerate panel is visible in the record. Must NOT be automated: choosing the proposal, marking the finding verified, running the panel on the coordinator's behalf (the window spend is the coordinator's decision), merging two proposals without recording merged_from, and the finder amending acceptance criteria after proposals exist. Pack contents: the located functions with their enclosing context, the tests in the same module, the finding record verbatim, and the invariant documentation - sanitised by the existing pack rules, hashed into pack_digest.

findings.claim: Q4 recommendation: score a signed ledger, not counters, and credit only verified outcomes with reversal on re-open. Solver +1 when the finding reaches verified; -1 if a later finding with the same trigger supersedes it. Finder +1 per finding that survives to verified, weighted by severity, and it may not rate the solver. Key solver score by (purpose, topic), not globally.
findings.trigger: A proposal is adopted, the fix lands, and the next pass either closes or re-opens the finding.

evidence.observation: Three pass-1 findings are marked still-open with a note that the pass-2 finding replaces the remaining claim - exactly the re-open event the scoring must reverse credit on.
Not read: whether ratings are stored as counters or as an append-only event log keyed by consult_id, which determines whether reversal is expressible without a migration.

findings.verification: Check the router's rating store for a per-consult_id event log; if it is a counter, reversal needs a signed entry, which is the design decision this finding asserts.
findings.remedy: Credit on verified, reverse on re-open, and require the reversal to reference the superseding finding id so the record shows why. Bounding easy-blocker gaming: weight by severity and require the coordinator to flag a finding's trigger as reachable, so a blocker with a trivial trigger earns little. Keep finder and solver scores in separate dimensions so a good solver with a mediocre finder record is routable as a solver.
